{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Southwestern cuisine|Southwestern cuisine]]

'''New Mexico Chile Verde''' is the most popular version of [[cookbook:chili con carne|chili con carne]] in the U.S. state of New Mexico. While there apparently is no canonical recipe for Chile Verde (''green chile''), <!--- that I have been able to find---> all versions involve roasting fresh green chile peppers and cooking them slowly with meat (usually [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] but also [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], or [[Cookbook:Turkey|turkey]]), [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], and [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]. The consistency is usually much thinner than Texas-style chili and is sometimes listed on restaurant menus as "green chile stew". In addition to being eaten by the bowl (sometimes with [[Cookbook:Pinto Bean|pinto beans]] or diced [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]] added), Chili Verde often is treated as a condiment and is ladled over [[Cookbook:Burrito|burritos]], [[Cookbook:Enchilada|enchiladas]], [[Cookbook:Hamburger|hamburgers]], and [[Cookbook:Fried Eggs|fried eggs]].

The following is a representative recipe for chili verde, but there are many variations:

==Ingredients==
*2 green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] (not frequently used in New Mexico)
*4 large, mild green [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chile peppers]]
*5 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*1 large can (16 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) stewed [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|bouillon]] granules
*1 tablespoon dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
*1 tablespoon whole [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]] seeds
*1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] ground [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*6 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]

==Procedure==
#Combine bell peppers, chili peppers, water, tomatoes, bouillon, oregano, cumin, and coriander in a large pot. Cook over medium heat until peppers are tender.
#Meanwhile, cook pork and onion in a [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] over medium heat, stirring occasionally, about ten minutes, or until pork is browned and crumbly. Drain pork and add to chile mixture. [[Cookbook:Simmer|Simmer]] for 20 minutes.
#Heat butter in the skillet over medium-low heat. Add flour. Cook, stirring frequently, until flour browns, about 2 minutes. 
#Add flour mixture to chile. Continue cooking and stirring until thickened to preference.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*If fresh green chili peppers are not available, dried [[Cookbook:Anaheim chili|Anaheim]] chili peppers may be substituted, but the results will be substantially different.
